name: Loading
description: Named progress and loading treatments for local, skeleton, and full-surface states.
usage:
<Spinner label="Saving" />
<Progress label="Import progress" value={64} />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-40" />
<LoadingState label="Loading reports" />

anatomy.description: role="status" glyph with an accessible label for local, short waits.
Determinate bar that exposes aria-valuenow for measurable work.
aria-hidden placeholder block that reserves the shape of incoming content.
Centered role="status" treatment that stands in for a whole region or panel.

dos: Match the treatment to the wait: Skeleton when the layout is known, Progress when it is measurable.
Give Spinner and LoadingState a label that names the work, such as "Saving".
donts: Don't show a spinner for operations that usually resolve instantly; it reads as flicker.
Don't layer Skeleton and Spinner over the same region at once.

examples.title: Loading treatments
examples.description: Spinner and Progress for active work, Skeleton for layout placeholders, LoadingState for regions.

examples.title: Skeleton region
examples.description: Reserve the eventual layout with Skeleton when content shape is known.

guidance.useWhen: Users need feedback while content or work is in progress.
guidance.avoidWhen: The operation is instant or no meaningful progress exists.
guidance.behavior: Use Spinner for local work, Skeleton for layout, and Progress for measurable work.
guidance.responsive: Prefer local indicators so small screens retain useful content.

notes: Spinner and LoadingState render role="status" with an accessible label, announced once to screen readers.
Progress exposes aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax through the Radix progress primitive.
Skeleton is aria-hidden because it duplicates content that is about to load.
